title: Site rescue
subtitle: Recovering a site whose infection has gone past the point where its files can be trusted

premise.title: Why replace instead of clean
premise.body: You can't prove a PHP file is clean — a good backdoor is indistinguishable from healthy code. But you can prove a file is identical to the official release. So nothing here is cleaned; files are replaced, and anything without an official source is your decision, never an automatic deletion.

backup.title: Snapshot
backup.desc: A full database backup before any change. The backup itself is infected — its purpose is not to restore the site, but to make going back possible.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.desc: Every plugin and theme sorted into one of three groups: replaceable from the repository, needs a clean copy from its vendor, or a folder that isn't a plugin at all.

leftovers.title: Hunt for leftovers
leftovers.desc: Places a core reinstall doesn't cover: PHP files in uploads, drop-ins, mu-plugins.

dbAudit.title: Database audit
dbAudit.desc: Admin users, hidden capabilities, infected options, and suspicious cron jobs. Report only — nothing is deleted.

rotateKeys.title: Rotate keys
rotateKeys.desc: If the attacker reached the database, they have the password hashes and session tokens. Without this step, all the work above is undone by tomorrow.

verify.title: Verify
verify.desc: Clean core, an empty scan, and no critical leftovers. Anything less than all three is a claim, not a result.

confirmRotate:
Rotating keys signs every user out of the site — including you.

A backup copy of wp-config.php is kept. Continue?

errors.queuedNoId: The step was queued, but no status id came back — run it again later.
errors.pollGaveUp: Reading the step's status failed several times. It is still running on the site — run it again later.
errors.failedOnSite: The step failed on the site.

result.dumpIncomplete: The dump is incomplete — don't rely on this backup.
